_comment:
Correction to a pillar C check first published in check set v1. This set exists because a published methodology never changes: 1.2.0 names only `v1`, `v1.1` and `v1.2` and must go on loading exactly what it always loaded, so a defect cannot be repaired by editing those directories. A later set supersedes an earlier definition of the same check id, and only a methodology version that names this set sees the correction.

What was wrong: a site that serves no plaintext HTTP at all matched no rule. The collector reaches the host successfully and records `http.redirect` as `observed` with `http_reachable: false`; the rules tested `redirects_to_https: true`, then `http_reachable: true`, then a `status: absent` that the normalizer never produces for this observation. Nothing matched, the check resolved to `unknown`, and the domain lost coverage.

The institution was penalised for the safer configuration. Refusing plaintext outright is strictly better than accepting it and redirecting, and the check exists to ask whether a visitor can be served over cleartext -- for these sites the answer is no, which is a pass. `not_applicable` was considered and rejected: it would drop the check from the score entirely and understate a deliberate, correct choice.

This is the third instance of one failure shape (see the v1.2 correction for the first two): a rule keyed on the observation status while the collector records a successful observation whose attribute carries the absent meaning. A test now replays every observation shape the collectors emit through the evaluator and fails on any check that matches no rule, so a fourth instance cannot reach a report unnoticed.

checks.rationale_ro: Vizitatorii care ajung pe HTTP trebuie mutați automat pe conexiunea securizată.
checks.rationale_en: Visitors arriving over HTTP must be moved automatically to the secure connection.
